| [ADR-054](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-054.md) v2 | Work is pushed to its pull request as it is made, and the pull request's CI repairs and lints it; contributors do not gate a push on running the record's checks locally | CLAUDE.md told contributors to run `luria repair`, `luria link --fix`, `luria index` and `luria lint` before every push. On a pull request the docs-check job already runs the repair, pushes it onto the branch, and lints the repaired tree, so the local run did the same work twice. At the record's present size it was also slow: on 2026-10-26 one local repair–link–lint pass ran past ten minutes, and work sat unpushed while it ran. At the owner's direction (2026-10-26), work is committed and pushed to its pull request as it is made. CI is the check, and a red check is read and fixed on the branch. `luria new` stays local, and a narrow local run is still allowed for diagnosing a red check. Rejected: keeping the local gate, a local lint only, and pushing straight to the default branch. | Active |
| [ADR-110](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-110.md) v2 | A postmortem is due when a schema change has been used, a batch of pull requests closes, a bulk filing lands, a decision is revised soon after landing, a process incident is fixed, or the owner asks; triggers count use and sessions, not calendar time, and a starting policy expected to be superseded | The owner asked on 2026-11-20 when to write a postmortem: not for every pull request, but perhaps for batches. Six triggers, measured in use and in working sessions because the record moves at about ten pull requests, one to five hundred entries and two decisions a day: a change to luria.yaml once about 20 entries use it or at the close of the first session that used it; a batch of five or more pull requests in a session, or any stack that had to be folded; a bulk filing of more than about 50 generated entries; a decision revised within the session it landed or the next; a process incident, once fixed; the owner's request. Not routine single filings that go green first time, nor the bot's repairs. The assistant checks the triggers when a batch closes and proposes; the owner decides. Short form for batches and incidents, the full form for schema changes. The owner expects this to be superseded: it is a starting policy, to be revised as postmortems show what is worth reviewing. Rejected: a postmortem per pull request; calendar intervals; leaving it to ad hoc request. | Proposed |

| [ADR-128](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-128.md) v2 | A pull request description that several writers edit is divided into marked sections, each kept by one writer, and every edit reads the description just before writing and writes only if it has not changed since | At the owner's go of 2026-11-21 ("lgtm") on the elaboration of the fourth recommendation of the retrospective of that day (pull request 600). The promotion pull request's description had three writers: the workflow, and two sessions. One session rebuilt it from its own picture of the batch, and the list of choices waiting on the owner, which it had not written, was lost without anyone deciding to drop it. Shared descriptions are now divided into sections opened by markers. Each writer edits its own sections and copies the rest through unchanged. | [ADR-132](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-132.md) v2 | When a hold the owner set lifts, the assistant says its next step and takes it in the same turn | At the owner's go of 2026-11-21 on the fifth recommendation of the retrospective of that day. The owner had held merges into staging until a promotion merged ("let's hold off on merging more stuff into staging until we've merged 582 into main first"). When it did, the assistant reported what was waiting but neither said what it would do next nor did it, and the owner had to ask: "you gonna open a new PR on staging or what?" A hold is a condition on the assistant's own next step. When the condition is met, the turn that sees it met names the step the hold was holding and takes it, unless the step is one that waits on the owner anyway. Rejected: asking the owner whether to resume, which turns a lifted hold into a new permission handoff. | Active |
| [ADR-137](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-137.md) v2 | Filing a source fills the gaps it leaves in its own argument, in the assistant's voice, without offering first | At the owner's request of 2026-11-21, after the filing of the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws" had been asked to fill the gaps it found: "update the skill instructions (via ADR) to include the gap filling instruction". A gap is a step the source's own argument needs and does not supply. The idea ledger records the gaps item by item, and the filing fills each real one in the assistant's voice, as a Proposed entry: a checked derivation, a correction, a question, or a lead for what would settle it. What cannot be filled is listed as left, with the reason. This is part of every filing of an exchange, synthesis or upload, not only when asked. Gap fills are filed without offering first; ideas only the whole filing shows (step 12) are still offered first. Rejected: filling gaps only on request, offering each gap fill first, and folding gap fills into step 12. | Active |
